speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; I see you are a newborn with increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. To determine the cause of this jaundice, have you noticed if the baby is feeding well, has had normal stool color, or appears lethargic?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (likely due to insufficient intake/dehydration) or early onset Breast Milk Jaundice. Given the age (2 weeks) and exclusively breastfed status, we must rule out biliary atresia (pale stools) and hemolytic disease. REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_Total_Serum, Bilirubin_Direct_Serum, Blood_Type, and Coombs_test. Please confirm stool color is not clay/pale and urine is not dark.
